tier1.text: The nucleus is the cell's control center because it stores the genetic instructions for making proteins. These instructions are kept in DNA, the cell's genetic material. The nucleus is wrapped in the nuclear envelope, a double membrane with pores that let materials in and out. Red blood cells have no nucleus, because they push it out as they mature.

sentences.text: The nucleus is the cell's control center because it stores the genetic instructions for making proteins.

quotes.quote: The nucleus is generally considered the control center of the cell because it stores all of the genetic instructions for manufacturing proteins.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: These instructions are kept in DNA, the cell's genetic material.

quotes.quote: Inside the nucleus lies the blueprint that dictates everything a cell will do and all of the products it will make. This information is stored within DNA.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: Threads of chromatin in the nucleus contain deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the genetic material of the cell.
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Cell Structure. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

sentences.text: The nucleus is wrapped in the nuclear envelope, a double membrane with pores that let materials in and out.

quotes.quote: The nucleus is encased within a membrane of two interconnected lipid bilayers, side-by-side. This nuclear envelope is studded with protein-lined pores that allow materials to be trafficked into and out of the nucleus.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: nuclear envelope: double-membrane structure that constitutes the nucleus' outermost portion
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Red blood cells have no nucleus, because they push it out as they mature.

quotes.quote: Other cells, such as mammalian red blood cells (RBCs), do not contain nuclei at all. RBCs eject their nuclei as they mature, making space for the large numbers of hemoglobin molecules that carry oxygen throughout the body ().
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
